Bed.name: Medical Bed
Bed.description:
Halewright knows there is no convenient place aboard a working ship for someone to get hurt. The Ward-3 makes a place for them to rest: a three-by-five sickbay bed weighing {0} kg, with dressings, splints and medicines kept in a drawer at the head.

An unconscious casualty can be laid here; an injured crewmate can rest awake, or use it for sleep. With power and a pressurised room, the bed keeps a patient recuperating at {1} kW. Without power it is an ordinary bed. Supplies and treatment still matter. A berth for the patient buys the crew somewhere to begin looking after their own.

Panel.help: Lay an unconscious casualty here while dragging them, or order an injured crew member to Rest and recover. Anyone tired may Sleep here unless you keep the bed for the injured. While powered and in air, the patient recuperates with the game's own medical-rest healing; cut the power and that stops until it returns. A resting patient gets up once their injuries have eased. Switch on Send injured crew here and the bed calls the worst-off injured crew member when it is free. A Vigil-2 monitor standing beside the bed shows the patient's readings and warns when they get worse.

Monitor.name: Patient Monitor
Monitor.description:
A change at the bedside should reach the watch before it becomes another surprise. Halewright's Vigil-2 keeps the Ward-3 patient in view, reporting blood lost, infection, pain and wounds, with the change over the last hour and crew-log warnings when a condition worsens.

The two-by-two cart weighs {0} kg and draws {1} kW while watching. Stand it touching the bed and read the Control Panel. The Vigil observes; it neither treats nor heals. It gives the crew information, and leaves the next act of care in their hands.
